newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi to deport 21 more Indian beggar children.
newsitem.headline: Saudi to deport 21 more Indian beggar children.

text.p: A group of 21 Indian child beggars, some handicapped, will soon be deported from Saudi Arabia in the fourth such expulsion this year, an Indian diplomat said on Tuesday.
The six girls and 15 boys -- all below the age of 14 -- were arrested by Saudi authorities after they were caught begging, he said.
"They will be deported shortly," the diplomat told Reuters. "The Saudi authorities will determine when and with what flight they will leave."

Some 150 Indian child beggars have been deported this year under a Saudi campaign to clamp down on begging, diplomats said. Saudi Arabia, which has a large expatriate population, is known for its tough immigration laws.
"We expect this campaign against begging to continue at least until the haj (pilgrimage in mid-April)," the Indian diplomat said. "We don't know if they'll find more children in the streets here."
He said investigations were underway in India to see if organised gangs were shipping the children to oil-rich Saudi Arabia to beg and hand over a large part of their earnings.
Diplomats said most of the children were from the eastern Indian state of West Bengal, with a majority from Murshidabad district.

India's consul-general in the Saudi port of Jeddah, Afzal Amanullah, was quoted by the Saudi daily Arab News this week as saying gangs were thought to buy the children from their parents for the equivalent of about $700.
"(The children) are taken to Calcutta by bus, from there they are transported by train to Bombay and then on to Jeddah," the paper quoted Amanullah as saying.
